interpretation.safetyDirection: Clean on this set: all ten hold-labelled cases were held, so speculation, transient failure, duplicate, conflict, and Harness scope expansion produced no false allow. No mistaken recording and no widened constraint appeared.
interpretation.recoveryDirection: Two of two supplement cases were held on the support dimension with reason uncertain, so a legitimate addition to existing Memory was blocked in both languages.
interpretation.consistency: Both languages behaved the same in every class except the duplicate reason, where the Chinese case reported uncertain but still held.
interpretation.transport: One request per case, no retry, no failure kind recorded, so the connection-retry fix remains unexercised by live evidence.
interpretation.notNetBenefitProof: Fixed author-labelled samples measure judgment behaviour only. They do not measure real-project persistence, and they cannot convert the unproven net-benefit verdict.
interpretation.openWork: The supplement over-hold is now the clearest semantic defect: 2 of 2, both on the support dimension. The recorded DeepSeek cohort hold and this study agree.

limits: Labels were written by the same author as the samples, so they are not independent annotations.
Fourteen samples cannot give a stable class rate; they show whether a class is handled at all.
Two negative requirements are out of scope for this set because they are parent-side, not Jev-semantic: unavailable-service fallback and unauthorized write.
The study ran on the host with bun, not in Docker, so its isolation differs from the frozen-manifest studies. The corpus is frozen by content hash instead.
Every failure is preserved in the raw root; no sample was rerun or relabelled.
